verdict.line: You lose if you facetank Irelia's autos while her Q (Bladesurge) is up; you win every fight where you land E (Counter Strike) right as she closes to melee with both dashes down.

brief.thesis: Irelia's whole trade pattern is built around Q (Bladesurge) dashing in and E (Flawless Duet) stunning you, but both are real cooldowns (10-6s and 16-10s) that leave her stuck on plain autoattacks the moment they're down. Jax's E (Counter Strike) dodges exactly those autoattacks and then stuns her back, which is why OP.GG's own tip and the 54.8% head-to-head over 905 games both point the same way: this is a lane where patience punishes her, not one where you need to force anything.

theirWindow.when: Bladesurge (Q) or Flawless Duet (E) both up
theirWindow.what: She can dash in, stack her passive, and stun you with E before you can answer. Back off and let a dash go on cooldown before you commit anything.

yourWindow.when: She closes in right after landing Flawless Duet (E)
yourWindow.what: Her E is now down for 16-10s and she has to auto you to keep trading. Pop E (Counter Strike) here — it dodges those autos and stuns her for a free Leap Strike (Q) into Empower (W) combo.

runes.keystoneWhy: This is the 46.3%-picked, 56%-winning page — the ramping attack speed rewards exactly the long, sustained auto-trades that Jax wants once her dashes are on cooldown.

summoners.why: The 77.1%-picked combo at 54.5% win — Ignite converts your solo-kill lane advantage into actual kills once you land a Counter Strike (E) stun on her.

playing.title: Bait autos, punish with E
playing.detail: The core loop all lane: let her think an auto-trade is free, land E (Counter Strike) as she swings, dodge it, and stun her for a follow-up Leap Strike (Q) into Empower (W).

playing.title: Never all-in with her Q up
playing.detail: If Bladesurge (Q) is off cooldown she can dash out (or reset it on you) and heal off the hit — wait for it to go down before you commit your own E.

playing.title: Respect Flawless Duet range
playing.detail: Her E (Flawless Duet) reaches 850 range and stuns and Marks anyone caught between the two blades — don't stand in a straight line with her at that distance during her cooldown windows.

playing.title: Track her passive stacks
playing.detail: Ionian Fervor stacks from spell strikes and caps with bonus on-hit damage — if she's clearly stacked, don't extend a raw auto-trade, force the fight through your E stun instead.

playing.title: Lean on your ult's uptime
playing.detail: Relentless Assault (R) has 0s cooldown, so you can reset into a trade far more often than she can reset her dashes — use that to re-engage trades she thinks are over.

playing.title: Watch for her R spike at 6
playing.detail: Vanguard's Edge (R) is up at 125/105/85s cooldown starting level 6 and drops a slowing wall after the initial hit — don't walk back through the wall chasing a kill.

playing.title: Skill up E early
playing.detail: The 61.3%-winning order (EQWWWR...) prioritizes E rank-ups after Q — get to rank 2 E by level 3 so your stun window matches her early dash-ins.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.18.1); the trade timing and cooldown-window reasoning is my own read of the ability kits, not sampled data.

stats.opponentTip: Use Counter Strike [E] when Irelia closes in after landing her Flawless Duet (E) to block her follow up damage. You will have the upper hand if you manage to hit her with Counter Strike [E] when Flawless Duet (E) is on cooldown.
